It takes real courage to name what you're going through, and living with anxiety that follows you everywhere can be exhausting. The good news is that anxiety is very treatable, and there are things that genuinely help over time.

A few approaches worth trying: practice slow breathing (breathe in for 4, out for 6) when you notice your body tensing up, since this signals your nervous system to calm down. Gentle movement, regular sleep, and limiting caffeine can also make a real difference. When anxious thoughts spiral, try naming them and asking, "Is this fact or fear?"—it can create a little distance.

That said, when anxiety is constant across school, home, and social life, talking to a professional can be a game-changer. A counselor or doctor can help you find strategies tailored to you, and approaches like therapy (CBT especially) work well for exactly this. If your school has a counselor, that's a good, low-pressure place to start. You don't have to carry this alone.
